session_summary: Built and debugged nested micro-agent dispatch on a Windows host. Shipped on branch voltron/nested-dispatch (unpushed): v3.8.0 nested dispatch (MCP-in-container + DooD socket), v3.8.1 socket-permission fix, v3.8.2 rename reflection-processor->harness-engineer, v3.8.3 -v->--mount fix. Also merged PR #31 and researched an LLM-as-judge testing harness. Nested 3-tier dispatch is now believed working but unvalidated pending a Claude Code restart. 2-tier dispatch worked flawlessly throughout.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Correctly handled large multi-file Voltron edits and self-rename; always halted cleanly and reported when nested dispatch was unavailable rather than falling back.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: Tasks that bundled 'edit + verify + commit' hit max_turns ~4 times this session, with the COMMIT always the casualty (work done, uncommitted). Separately, every run on this Windows repo flipped CRLF->LF line endings on touched files, creating noisy diffs and once burning ~8 turns fighting it.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: Split 'commit' out as its own step/dispatch by default rather than bundling it into a large edit task. Add a line-endings rule to the harness-engineer template: never normalize EOLs; rely on git autocrlf; if a file shows an EOL-only diff, git checkout -- it. Consider adding a repo .gitattributes to end the churn.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Exemplary tier discipline: dispatched to micro-agents, and on dispatch failure STOPPED and reported the verbatim error every time instead of writing files itself.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: Nothing — behavior was exactly as intended.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Parallel-safe orchestration, bead tracking, and anchor pre-computation before file-edit dispatches.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: When dispatching any Voltron-edit task, default to a separate committer dispatch for the commit; do not let edit+commit share one turn budget.

overall_notes: Nested-dispatch design under-specified Windows Docker: needed 3 fixes after the initial build — socket permission (non-root user can't read mounted socket; fixed with sudo + a docker wrapper), and `-v` mount parsing (Windows `C:\` drive-colon breaks the Linux docker CLI's `-v` splitter; fixed by switching all mounts to `--mount type=bind`). Future DooD work on Windows should mandate `--mount` syntax and address socket perms up front. Also: every run_agent_in_docker result exceeded the inline token limit and had to be parsed from a saved file — consistent minor friction. Any change to src/index.js or templates.js requires a full Claude Code restart to take effect, which makes iterating on dispatch internals slow — worth noting in contributor docs.
